problem_statement: In Caliptra's KeyVault read client (`kv_read_client`), the status for a multi-beat read transaction can be overwritten by a later beat instead of preserving an earlier failure. If a KeyVault read stays active across multiple beats and one non-final beat reports a read error, a subsequent successful beat, including the final beat, can incorrectly make the overall transaction appear successful. `kv_read_client` is the block that returns KeyVault data to Caliptra hardware consumers. The expected behavior is that once any beat in a read transaction reports a KeyVault read failure, that failure remains latched for the rest of the transaction and the completed read reports failure rather than success.

resolved_issues.title: [RTL] Keyvault controls need to be locked during operation
resolved_issues.body:
During crypto engine operation we want keyvault controls to be locked so that filtering rules can't be bypassed.

This also prevents potential malicious behavior like changing entries, or performing reads from the keyvault during engine operation.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) engine, software can still rewrite the KeyVault private-key read-control register after an ECC signing operation has started. KeyVault is Caliptra's internal key storage interface used by crypto blocks to fetch protected key material. When ECC signing is configured to use a private key from a KeyVault entry, the selected entry must remain fixed for the entire signing operation. If software writes a different value to the ECC KeyVault private-key control register while the ECC engine is busy, that write should be ignored and the signature should still be generated from the key that was selected before the operation began. Instead, the active KeyVault private-key selection can change mid-operation, which changes the ECC signing result.

problem_statement: In Caliptra 2.0, the VeeR EL2 RISC-V core's AXI4-to-AHB bridge mishandles back-to-back read requests on the load/store path. If one read is followed immediately by another and the AHB-Lite slave deasserts HREADY while the second request is being presented, the bridge can change that second transfer from a valid AHB NONSEQ read to the wrong transfer type and can lose the low address bits of the buffered request. As a result, the second read can appear on AHB at an aligned or otherwise incorrect address instead of the requested address. The correct behavior is to keep the stalled second read as a valid NONSEQ transfer and preserve its exact requested address, including the low address bits, until the AHB slave accepts it.

resolved_issues.title: uds_seed/field_entropy hw-load is able to bypass CPTRA_FUSE_WR_DONE
Bug: ahb_slv_sif continues to assert 'dv' after an error response is received
resolved_issues.body:
This occurs due to the AHB signalling protocol. 
hreadyout is 0 for 1 cycle while hresp = 1. 
Current logic uses hready_i to clear the 'dv' signal or load a new request in from AHB, but that causes pending transactions to be resent on the component interface.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's `ahb_slv_sif` block, which bridges the AMBA Advanced High-performance Bus (AHB) to an internal client request interface, the downstream request-valid signal `dv` remains asserted for one extra clock after an outstanding transfer receives an error response. The bug is triggered when an AHB transfer has already been accepted, the internal client holds the request for at least one cycle, and then the client reports an error during the first AHB error-response cycle while the AHB bus is still not ready. The observed incorrect behavior is that `dv` stays high on that error cycle instead of clearing. The expected behavior is that as soon as the outstanding request completes with an error, `dv` must deassert in that same cycle and remain low until a new valid AHB transfer is accepted.

resolved_issues.title: Simultaneous AXI Read and Write transactions cause incorrect arbitration in subordinate_arb
resolved_issues.body:
The problem happens when the arbiter gets the Read and Write transaction in the same clock cycle. The arbiter is supposed to prioritize Write over Read, however if both of them happen at the same time, the arbiter issues two writes (with the same data) to the underlying logic and the Read is lost.

This issue has been fixed in the i3c-core (which uses the same subordinate AXI arbiter) with https://github.com/chipsalliance/i3c-core/commit/676fc8ed5c38aa4aa61f07988c7dc5303bc03be1

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

BASE_SHA="d1a3be59fdadce8169398fd77acc717dc33d282c"

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace.
cd /home/caliptra-rtl
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx

if ! git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  git fetch --depth=1 origin "${BASE_SHA}"
fi

git checkout "${BASE_SHA}"

# Stage 2: sync submodules to the checked-out commit.
git submodule sync --recursive || true
git submodule update --init --recursive || true

# Normalize the one CRLF source file touched by fix.patch so the runtime-mounted
# LF patch applies cleanly inside the harness.
perl -0pi -e 's/\r\n/\n/g' src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv

# Stage 3: detect tool versions from the checked-out repo and align the environment.
verilator_version="v5.044"
riscv_version="v12.1.0"
workflow_file=".github/workflows/build-test-verilator.yml"

if [[ -f "$workflow_file" ]]; then
  detected_verilator="$(awk -F': ' '/^[[:space:]]+VERILATOR_VERSION:/ {gsub(/"/, "", $2); print $2; exit}' "$workflow_file")"
  detected_riscv="$(awk -F': ' '/^[[:space:]]+RISCV_VERSION:/ {gsub(/"/, "", $2); print $2; exit}' "$workflow_file")"
  if [[ -n "$detected_verilator" ]]; then
    verilator_version="$detected_verilator"
  fi
  if [[ -n "$detected_riscv" ]]; then
    riscv_version="$detected_riscv"
  fi
fi

echo "[INFO] Requested Verilator version: ${verilator_version}"
echo "[INFO] Requested RISC-V toolchain version: ${riscv_version}"

if ! command -v verilator >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! verilator --version | head -n1 | grep -q "${verilator_version#v}"; then
  /usr/local/bin/install-verilator-version "${verilator_version}"
fi

if ! command -v riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1 | grep -q "${riscv_version#v}"; then
  /usr/local/bin/install-caliptra-riscv-toolchain "${riscv_version}"
fi

hash -r

# Stage 4: install minimal Python deps used by the open-source smoke/regression scripts.
python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel pyyaml
python -m pip show pyyaml >/dev/null

if [[ ! -f tools/scripts/Makefile ]]; then
  echo "[ERROR] tools/scripts/Makefile not found at ${BASE_SHA}"
  exit 1
fi

verilator --version | head -n1
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1
python --version
problem_statement: In Caliptra's AXI subordinate arbiter (`axi_sub_arb`), overlapping read and write traffic can be arbitrated incorrectly when a read request has already been selected but is still blocked by downstream backpressure. If a write request becomes valid in the same cycle that the downstream hold is released, the arbiter can switch to the write too early and the pending read can be lost. This affects the AXI block that merges read and write requests onto a shared downstream request interface. The expected behavior is testable: once a read or write beat has won arbitration, that winner must remain selected until the downstream interface actually accepts that beat; only after the accepted transfer completes may the arbiter apply its normal write-over-read priority to choose the next request. Under this trigger condition, the stalled read must complete first, and the write may be issued only afterward.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's AES control finite-state machine, AES-GCM manual operation is not correctly enforced during the GCM TAG phase. When AES-GCM is configured for manual start, the controller is in the TAG phase, and software has already written a complete input block for tag processing, the block can leave its idle state and begin the GHASH (Galois hash) side of tag handling before software issues the explicit START command. The correct behavior is that manual mode must keep the AES-GCM TAG phase idle until START is asserted; loading the full tag input block alone must not consume that input or begin tag processing. This bug affects the AES subsystem's GCM control path under the trigger condition of manual operation plus a fully loaded TAG-phase input block.

problem_statement: In the Caliptra SHA-512 accelerator, the generate Platform Configuration Register (PCR) hash flow can leave the message-block lock state stuck after the operation finishes. If software runs a generate-PCR-hash command, waits for completion, issues a zeroize, and then starts a normal SHA-512 hash, the SHA-512 block registers can still behave as locked and fail to accept the newly written message block. The following standard SHA-512 command can therefore return an incorrect digest. Zeroize is expected to fully clear any lock state created by the generate-PCR-hash flow so that the next standard SHA-512 command behaves like a fresh operation: newly written block data must be accepted and the digest must match that data. The affected subsystem is the SHA-512 block, specifically the interaction between the generate-PCR-hash path and zeroize recovery.

title: Crypto enhancement
body:
Enhanced crypto modules including:
1) remove deadcode in doe_core_cbc (found by FPV)
dead code in line 254-255 doe_core_cbc.sv:
                    else if(enc_ready)
                        IV_enc_state <= st_IV_engine_idle;

2) froze adder inputs to fix #194 (found by FPV)
With this PR, there is no more constraints on keeping inputs fixed. The only constraint is having a single pulse add_en_i, and do not enable it again until ready_o.

3) remove sca_en_i since countermeasures are hardcoded to be enabled (found by FPV)

4) remove deadcode in ecc_pm_ctrl:163 (found by FPV)
in ecc_pm_ctrl:163 the last else if () is always taken. This PR switches to just else to avoid confusion.

5) Stop faulty ECC from continuing before zeroize (found by FPV): When the error happens for the first time, the error flag goes high and will remain high until zeroize. We expect that uC issues zeroize if there is an error in ECC. In this scenario, although the second command will be performed, the results should not be used since error flag is kept high. However, this PR stops faulty ECC from continuing before zeroize.

6) removed one cycle delay for hmac_drbg ready (found by FPV)
This PR synchronizes hmac_drbg READY to VALID by removing one cycle delay

7) add all_1 protection for LFSR
This PR has protection for the LFSR to stuck to be all 1.

8) Remove zeroize for the counter used as countermeasure (found by IOActive)

In line 300 of scalar_blinding, we have a loop of 20 iterations (0 to 19). However, when we enter the last round, the scalar blinding flag changes to done and we don't perform the last iteration. This PR reduces the iteration by one by updating FULL_DIG_NUM.

resolved_issues.title: [ECC] add_sub_mod_alter ready not aligned with result
resolved_issues.body:
Hello, 

We found an issue with the ready signal which does not align with the computed result. The expected behaviour of the ready signal is to be set when we have the correct result. In the current implementation the ready arrives 1-2 cycles, if and only if the enable signal is kept low. 

@mojtaba-bisheh confirmed this issue, however, the design works fine with the current implementation, because it does not affect the computation itself. It will be updated in future releases.  

We adde two sets of constraints for this module. One that includes the intended input behaviour and one that fixes the current issues appended with _bugfix. Please remove that constraint after the RTL design updates are done to check for correctness. 

Best
Tobias

problem_statement: In Caliptra's ECC modular add/subtract helper `ecc_add_sub_mod_alter`, a request is not fully captured when `add_en_i` is pulsed. If software or surrounding logic starts an operation with a single-cycle `add_en_i` pulse and then changes `sub_i`, the operands, or the modulus before `ready_o` asserts, the block can raise `ready_o` while `res_o` reflects the newer input values instead of the original transaction. The correct behavior is that each launched operation is self-contained: after a single `add_en_i` pulse, `ready_o` must indicate that `res_o` is valid for the operation mode, operands, and modulus that were present when the request was accepted, and callers should not need to keep those inputs fixed until completion as long as no new operation is issued before `ready_o`.

title: [entropy_src] Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow
body:
Keep applying fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow instead of pulsing. This commit is a manual port of the following Opentitan commit:

b454878f2528b49318ff2b604cb8d59a6e59b0ea

Which is associated with
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/21640.

Original commit description:

This commit applies the fw_ov_rd_fifo_overflow signal in case of an overflow. It used to only send a pulse through the register but now the signal is applied until the FIFO has been emptied once and is receiving contiguous data again.
This commit also aligns the documentation for the FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW register. The register is now not clearable by software. It instead is cleared by hardware.

Fixes: https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-rtl/issues/503

resolved_issues.title: sfifo_observe_gate_q is stuck at reset in entropy_src
resolved_issues.body: This register sfifo_observe_gate_q never gets out of reset because the set condition can't ever be true. The observe push is qualified by the observe full already, so we never detect when there was an attempt to push the fifo while it was full.

problem_statement: In Caliptra's `entropy_src` block, the firmware-override observe FIFO overflow indicator is not held in a stable, software-visible state. The observe FIFO is the buffer that lets firmware read raw entropy samples through `FW_OV_RD_DATA`. When firmware override mode is enabled and new entropy samples keep arriving after that FIFO has become full, `FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` can appear only as a pulse instead of staying asserted. As a result, firmware can miss the fact that samples were dropped and cannot reliably tell whether the data it reads from `FW_OV_RD_DATA` is still a contiguous stream of samples. The expected behavior is that once the firmware-override observe FIFO overflows, `FW_OV_RD_FIFO_OVERFLOW` remains asserted on repeated reads until the observe FIFO has been completely drained and sampling has restarted with contiguous data again; only then should the status clear.
